title: Wordle was made for one person
hook: The word game millions play each morning was first a present for one person.
peek: Josh Wardle made Wordle for his partner, Palak Shah, who loves word games. She helped pick its answers. Shared with the world in October 2021, it went from a few dozen players to millions within months.
lede: Josh Wardle, a software engineer in New York, built a simple word-guessing game for his partner, Palak Shah, during the pandemic. The name was a pun on his surname. For months the two played it privately, along with his family. In October 2021 he put it online for anyone, with no ads and one puzzle a day.

bullets.text: The English language has around 12,000 five-letter words, many of them obscure. Wardle had Shah sort through them, and she kept roughly 2,500 that she actually knew, which became the answer list.
Players in New Zealand began sharing their results as rows of coloured emoji squares, giving away nothing about the word. Wardle liked the idea and built a share button that did it for them.
On 1 November 2021, about 90 people played. By January 2022 it had millions of players, almost entirely through those shared grids.
In January 2022 the New York Times bought Wordle for a price in the low seven figures. It still sets one shared puzzle a day, and a human editor now chooses the answers.
